# kopia_effective_policy (Data Source)

Resolves the policy Kopia applies to a target: its own policy merged with everything it inherits, from the policies of its parent directories up to `(global)` and Kopia's built-in defaults. It also tells which target each value comes from, and when the server will take the next snapshots, as Kopia's UI shows them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# What Kopia applies to a source: its own policy merged with everything it
# inherits. The target needs no policy of its own.
data "kopia_effective_policy" "postgres" {
  target                      = "docker@host1:/srv/postgres"
  num_upcoming_snapshot_times = 3
}

output "postgres_keep_daily" {
  value = data.kopia_effective_policy.postgres.effective.retention.keep_daily
}

# Which policy each value comes from; "(global)" also stands for Kopia's
# built-in defaults.
output "postgres_cron_from" {
  value = lookup(data.kopia_effective_policy.postgres.definition, "scheduling.cron", null)
}

output "postgres_next_snapshots" {
  value = data.kopia_effective_policy.postgres.upcoming_snapshot_times
}

# Warn on every plan when Kopia would refuse the schedule, or when the source
# would never be snapshotted on a schedule.
check "postgres_is_scheduled" {
  assert {
    condition     = data.kopia_effective_policy.postgres.scheduling_error == null
    error_message = "Kopia refuses the schedule: ${coalesce(data.kopia_effective_policy.postgres.scheduling_error, "unknown")}"
  }

  assert {
    condition     = length(data.kopia_effective_policy.postgres.upcoming_snapshot_times) > 0
    error_message = "docker@host1:/srv/postgres has no upcoming scheduled snapshot."
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `target` (String) Target to resolve, written as for `kopia_policy`: `(global)`, `@host`, `user@host` or `user@host:path`, such as the path of a snapshot source. It needs no policy of its own.

### Optional

- `num_upcoming_snapshot_times` (Number) Number of upcoming snapshot times to compute, from 0 to 100. Defaults to `0`.

### Read-Only

- `definition` (Map of String) Where each value of `effective` comes from: the target whose policy sets it, keyed by the attribute's path, such as `retention.keep_daily` or `logging.entries.cache_hit`. `(global)` stands for the global policy or a built-in default, which Kopia does not tell apart. Kopia reports no source for `no_parent`, `scheduling.no_parent_time_of_day` and the `no_parent_*` flags of `compression`, which are left out; `actions.before_folder` and `actions.after_folder` are never inherited, so they come from `target` itself. `scheduling.time_of_day` names the most general policy that has times of day, even where `no_parent_time_of_day` excludes them.
- `effective` (Attributes) The effective policy, with the attributes of `kopia_policy`. An attribute nothing sets is null, and so is a section with nothing set; `no_parent` is always null, as Kopia reports it only on the policies themselves. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective))
- `scheduling_error` (String) Why Kopia would refuse the target's own scheduling section, or null when it accepts it.
- `upcoming_snapshot_times` (List of String) The next times the server will take a snapshot of the target, as RFC 3339 timestamps in the server's time zone, computed as if a snapshot had just finished: they ignore `run_missed` and the snapshots actually taken. Empty when the schedule is manual or there is none, and when `num_upcoming_snapshot_times` is 0. The server schedules only sources on its own host.

<a id="nestedatt--effective"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective`

Read-Only:

- `actions` (Attributes) Commands run around snapshots. They run only if the server's repository connection has actions enabled (`kopia repository connect --enable-actions`); otherwise Kopia skips them. `before_snapshot_root` and `after_snapshot_root` are inherited, while `before_folder` and `after_folder` apply only to the directory of this very policy. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--actions))
- `compression` (Attributes) How file contents are compressed. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--compression))
- `error_handling` (Attributes) Which read errors a snapshot tolerates instead of failing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--error_handling))
- `files` (Attributes) Which files a snapshot leaves out. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--files))
- `logging` (Attributes) How much a snapshot logs about the directories and files it processes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--logging))
- `metadata_compression` (Attributes) How Kopia compresses the directory listings and other metadata of snapshots. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--metadata_compression))
- `no_parent` (Boolean) Whether this policy inherits nothing: neither from less specific policies nor Kopia's built-in defaults, so that whatever it leaves out falls back to Kopia's runtime behaviour, which, among other things, keeps every snapshot and compresses nothing. It also keeps this policy's own `before_folder` and `after_folder` actions from running at the root of a snapshot. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `os_snapshots` (Attributes) Operating-system snapshots taken of the source while it is read. Only Kopia servers on Windows take them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--os_snapshots))
- `retention` (Attributes) Which snapshots Kopia keeps when it expires old ones. Every `keep_*` count keeps the newest snapshot of each of that many hours, days, weeks, months or years, counted back from the newest snapshot, and `keep_latest` the newest snapshots overall; a snapshot any count keeps is kept. `0` is an explicit count that overrides what is inherited; if the six counts add up to 0, Kopia keeps every snapshot. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--retention))
- `scheduling` (Attributes) When the Kopia server takes snapshots by itself. It schedules only sources on its own host, and the next snapshot is the earliest of the interval, the times of day and the cron entries in effect, wherever each is set: an interval on a path does not replace a cron schedule it inherits, both apply. Times of day and cron entries are in the server's local time zone. The provider checks the section with Kopia at plan time, which is how an invalid cron entry is found before the apply. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--scheduling))
- `splitter` (Attributes) How files are split into chunks for deduplication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--splitter))
- `upload` (Attributes) How much of a snapshot runs in parallel. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--upload))

<a id="nestedatt--effective--actions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.actions`

Read-Only:

- `after_folder` (Attributes) Runs after a snapshot has left the directory this policy is defined on. Exactly one of `command` and `script` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--actions--after_folder))
- `after_snapshot_root` (Attributes) Runs after a snapshot has finished. Exactly one of `command` and `script` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--actions--after_snapshot_root))
- `before_folder` (Attributes) Runs before a snapshot enters the directory this policy is defined on. Exactly one of `command` and `script` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--actions--before_folder))
- `before_snapshot_root` (Attributes) Runs before a snapshot starts. Exactly one of `command` and `script` must be set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--actions--before_snapshot_root))

<a id="nestedatt--effective--actions--after_folder"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.actions.after_folder`

Read-Only:

- `args` (List of String) Arguments to `command`. Only valid together with `command`.
- `command` (String) Path of the program to run, on the Kopia server. Kopia sends it as `path`.
- `mode` (String) `essential`, where a non-zero exit status fails the snapshot (the default of `kopia policy set`), `optional`, where it is only logged, or `async`, where Kopia does not wait for the command. Kopia treats a mode it is not given as `optional`.
- `script` (String) Script to run instead of a command, at most 32000 bytes. Kopia writes it to a temporary file on the server and runs that directly when it starts with `#!`, with `sh -e` otherwise, or with `%COMSPEC% /c` on Windows.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Time limit in seconds; Kopia allows 3 minutes when it is not set. Kopia sends it as `timeout`.

- `command` (String) Path of the program to run, on the Kopia server. Kopia sends it as `path`.
- `mode` (String) `essential`, where a non-zero exit status fails the snapshot (the default of `kopia policy set`), `optional`, where it is only logged, or `async`, where Kopia does not wait for the command. Kopia treats a mode it is not given as `optional`.
- `script` (String) Script to run instead of a command, at most 32000 bytes. Kopia writes it to a temporary file on the server and runs that directly when it starts with `#!`, with `sh -e` otherwise, or with `%COMSPEC% /c` on Windows.
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Time limit in seconds; Kopia allows 3 minutes when it is not set. Kopia sends it as `timeout`.

<a id="nestedatt--effective--compression"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.compression`

Read-Only:

- `compressor_name` (String) Compression algorithm, such as `zstd`, `zstd-fastest` or `s2-default`, or `none`, which overrides a compressor inherited from above. Kopia's built-in default is `none`. The provider checks the name against the algorithms the server supports at plan time; `lz4` no longer works from Kopia 0.23 on.
- `max_size` (Number) Size in bytes above which files are not compressed, or `-1` for no limit, which overrides a limit inherited from above. Kopia cannot store `0`.
- `min_size` (Number) Size in bytes below which files are not compressed, or `-1` for no limit, which overrides a limit inherited from above. Kopia cannot store `0`.
- `never_compress` (Set of String) File extensions, with their leading dot, such as `.gz` or `.jpg`, that are never compressed. The extensions of every level are combined, unless `no_parent_never_compress` is set.
- `no_parent_never_compress` (Boolean) Whether the `never_compress` extensions of less specific policies are dropped. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `no_parent_only_compress` (Boolean) Whether the `only_compress` extensions of less specific policies are dropped. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `only_compress` (Set of String) File extensions, with their leading dot, such as `.txt`, that are compressed even when `never_compress` lists them. Despite its name it restricts nothing: files with other extensions are compressed too, unless `never_compress` lists them. Unlike other settings, the extensions of every level are combined, unless `no_parent_only_compress` is set.


<a id="nestedatt--effective--error_handling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.error_handling`

Read-Only:

- `ignore_directory_errors` (Boolean) Whether errors reading directories are ignored. Kopia's built-in default is `false`. Kopia 0.22 applies `ignore_file_errors` to directories too.
- `ignore_file_errors` (Boolean) Whether errors reading files are ignored. Kopia's built-in default is `false`.
- `ignore_unknown_types` (Boolean) Whether entries of unknown types, such as sockets, are skipped silently. Kopia's built-in default is `true`.


<a id="nestedatt--effective--files"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.files`

Read-Only:

- `ignore` (List of String) Ignore rules in `.gitignore` syntax, in order: a later rule overrides an earlier one, `!` includes a file again and `\` escapes the next character. Kopia compiles the rules only when it takes a snapshot, so a malformed one fails the snapshot, not the apply; the provider warns about a trailing `\` and an unclosed `[`. The most specific policy that sets a list replaces the lists of every policy above it; a more specific policy cannot clear it.
- `ignore_cache_dirs` (Boolean) Whether directories marked as caches by a `CACHEDIR.TAG` file are left out. Kopia treats it as `true` when no policy sets it.
- `ignore_dot_files` (List of String) Names of files, such as `.kopiaignore` (Kopia's built-in default) or `.gitignore`, whose rules a snapshot applies to the directory they are in. The most specific policy that sets a list replaces the lists of every policy above it; a more specific policy cannot clear it.
- `max_file_size` (Number) Size in bytes above which files are left out, or `-1` for no limit, which overrides a limit inherited from above. Kopia cannot store `0`.
- `no_parent_dot_files` (Boolean) Whether the ignore files of parent directories inside a snapshot are no longer applied. Once a policy sets it, more specific ones cannot clear it. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `no_parent_ignore` (Boolean) Whether ignore rules inherited from the parent directories inside a snapshot are dropped. Once a policy sets it, more specific ones cannot clear it. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `one_file_system` (Boolean) Whether a snapshot stays on the file system its root is on, leaving out other file systems mounted below it. Kopia treats it as `false` when no policy sets it.


<a id="nestedatt--effective--logging"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.logging`

Read-Only:

- `directories` (Attributes) Logging about directories. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--logging--directories))
- `entries` (Attributes) Logging about files and other entries. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--logging--entries))

<a id="nestedatt--effective--logging--directories"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.logging.directories`

Read-Only:

- `ignored` (Number) Detail logged for a directory left out. Kopia's built-in default is `5`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.
- `snapshotted` (Number) Detail logged for a directory snapshotted. Kopia's built-in default is `5`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.


<a id="nestedatt--effective--logging--entries"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.logging.entries`

Read-Only:

- `cache_hit` (Number) Detail logged for an entry found unchanged in the cache. Kopia's built-in default is `0`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.
- `cache_miss` (Number) Detail logged for an entry not found in the cache. Kopia's built-in default is `0`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.
- `ignored` (Number) Detail logged for an entry left out. Kopia's built-in default is `5`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.
- `snapshotted` (Number) Detail logged for an entry snapshotted. Kopia's built-in default is `0`. From 0 (nothing) to 10 (everything); 5 is normal.



<a id="nestedatt--effective--metadata_compression"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.metadata_compression`

Read-Only:

- `compressor_name` (String) Compression algorithm, or `none`. Kopia's built-in default is `zstd-fastest`. The provider checks the name at plan time, as for `compression`.


<a id="nestedatt--effective--os_snapshots"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.os_snapshots`

Read-Only:

- `volume_shadow_copy` (String) Whether Windows Volume Shadow Copy is used: `never` (Kopia's built-in default), `always`, which fails the snapshot when no shadow copy can be made, or `when-available`, which carries on without one and warns. A number Kopia stores that is none of these is shown as it is.


<a id="nestedatt--effective--retention"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.retention`

Read-Only:

- `ignore_identical_snapshots` (Boolean) Whether a snapshot identical to the previous one is discarded instead of saved. Kopia's built-in default is `false`.
- `keep_annual` (Number) Number of years to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `3`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_daily` (Number) Number of days to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `7`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_hourly` (Number) Number of hours to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `48`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_latest` (Number) Number of most recent snapshots to keep. Kopia's built-in default is `10`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_monthly` (Number) Number of months to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `24`. Between 0 and 2147483647.
- `keep_weekly` (Number) Number of weeks to keep the newest snapshot of. Kopia's built-in default is `4`. Between 0 and 2147483647.


<a id="nestedatt--effective--scheduling"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.scheduling`

Read-Only:

- `cron` (List of String) Cron expressions, such as `0 3 * * *`, at which to take a snapshot. Kopia treats everything from a `#` on as a comment, so cron's `#` syntax for the n-th weekday of a month cannot be used: `0 0 * * 5#3` runs every Friday. The provider warns about a `#` that does not follow a space. The most specific policy that sets a list replaces the lists of every policy above it; a more specific policy cannot clear it.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Interval between snapshots, in seconds. Snapshots are aligned to multiples of the interval counted in UTC, so `86400` takes one at midnight UTC. Kopia cannot store `0`, and a more specific policy cannot clear an inherited interval.
- `manual` (Boolean) Whether snapshots are only taken on request, never on a schedule. Kopia refuses it together with any other scheduling attribute, and once a policy sets it, more specific ones cannot clear it. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `no_parent_time_of_day` (Boolean) Whether the times of day of less specific policies are dropped, leaving only this policy's own, or none. Kopia cannot store `false` here: `false` and leaving the attribute out both mean that this policy does not set it, so it can turn the setting on but never off for what it inherits.
- `run_missed` (Boolean) Whether a snapshot at a time of day or cron time that was missed, while the server was down, say, is taken as soon as possible, provided the next one is more than 30 minutes away. It does not apply to intervals. Kopia's built-in default is `true`.
- `time_of_day` (Attributes Set) Times of day at which to take a snapshot. Unlike other settings, the times of every level are combined: a policy adds its own to those it inherits, unless `no_parent_time_of_day` is set. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--effective--scheduling--time_of_day))

<a id="nestedatt--effective--scheduling--time_of_day"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.scheduling.time_of_day`

Read-Only:

- `hour` (Number) Hour, from 0 to 23.
- `minute` (Number) Minute, from 0 to 59.



<a id="nestedatt--effective--splitter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.splitter`

Read-Only:

- `algorithm` (String) Splitter algorithm, such as `DYNAMIC-4M-BUZHASH` or `FIXED-1M`. Without one, the repository's own splitter is used. The provider checks the name against the algorithms the server supports at plan time; Kopia itself would fall back to the repository's splitter silently.


<a id="nestedatt--effective--upload"></a>
### Nested Schema for `effective.upload`

Read-Only:

- `max_parallel_file_reads` (Number) Number of files read at the same time. Kopia uses the number of CPUs when no policy sets it.
- `max_parallel_snapshots` (Number) Number of snapshots the server takes at the same time. Kopia's built-in default is `1`. Kopia reads it only from the policies of the server's own `user@host` and refuses it on a path policy, so it has no effect on other targets.
- `parallel_upload_above_size` (Number) Size in bytes above which a file is uploaded in parallel chunks, or a negative number never to. Kopia's built-in default is `2147483648` (2 GiB). `0` is refused: Kopia would divide by it.
